about: The priest asks God to make the offering blessed, duly recognized, ratified, spiritual and acceptable. The final petition asks that it may become for us the Body and Blood of God's dearly beloved Son, our Lord Jesus Christ.

s01.translation: O God, we ask You graciously to make this offering in all respects

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

s02.narrative: The priest makes three signs of the cross over the offerings.

s03.translation: blessed, duly recognized, ratified, spiritual, and acceptable to You:

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

s04.narrative: The priest makes one sign of the cross over the Host alone, at the word Corpus, and one over the chalice alone, at Sanguis.

s05.translation: so that for us it may become the Body and Blood of Your dearly beloved Son,

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)
The Missal for the Use of the Laity (1853)

w003.explanation: The expressed subject pronoun, which Latin usually omits, emphasizes the addressee named immediately as “Deus” (w004).

w017.explanation: The understood subject is the “oblátio” introduced at the beginning of the prayer, so the verb is singular.
